newsitem.title: CHINA: China metal exchanges mull copper contract merger.
newsitem.headline: China metal exchanges mull copper contract merger.

text.p: Two of China's metals exchanges are considering merging their copper contracts so spot prices can more accurately reflect the national market, Chinese traders said on Friday.
The Shanghai and Shenyang exchanges now trade the same six copper contracts but regulate them differently, applying divergent delivery standards and limit-up and limit-down rules, the traders said.
Officials at the Shanghai exchange, China's biggest and most influential metals trading floor, were not available for comment.
Officials at the less active Shenyang exchange in far northern Liaoning province delined to comment.
The Shenyang exchange was likely to revise its regulations to coincide with Shanghai's so investors could trade and deliver without any barriers between the two exchanges, a trader said.

"With the current different regulations, trading on the two exchanges is separate and so they do not operate like a large-scale market in reflecting the nationwide spot market situation," another trader said.
Traders said uniting the two markets would boost trading activity, especially in Shenyang, and improve the credibility of the Shanghai exchange in reflecting and discovering spot prices.

"Because the Shanghai exchange is (closer to) southern China, it cannot fully reflect supply and demand in the northern markets, and that weakens its authority in deciding the spot price," another trader said.
"The unification could provide the Shanghai exchange with more timely information from the northern markets and make it more influential," he said.
"The Shenyang market is small compared with Shanghai and so it will benefit from the unification because market liquidity would be increased," another trader said.
Copper futures contracts are traded on six exchanges in China, but only four exchanges had trading volume, traders said.
